passage: Coordinator's note, community centre. I'm Yamini, and I'm writing down what I saw Kalyani do, because it was quicker than most of us manage. Kalyani had drafted a one-page guide for new volunteers. It was good but not polished: one paragraph was clumsy, and the map was hand-drawn. Instead of holding it for another week, Kalyani printed five copies and gave them to two volunteers, the caretaker and me with a line at the top: “Version one. Tell me what's wrong.” Within two days we had eleven comments, mostly about the map and the opening hours. Kalyani fixed those and posted version two on the noticeboard on Friday. I would have waited a month.

qa.a: Kalyani seems comfortable and practical rather than anxious, treating the rough version as a way to learn what needs fixing.

qa.a: Kalyani fixed the map and opening hours and posted version two on the noticeboard on Friday.

grounding: A worker ships a good-enough version, gathers feedback and improves it instead of waiting for perfection.

passage: Saturday. Today I sent Ramesh the first draft of the housing society newsletter, eight pages, at about sixty percent: two photos missing, the back page empty. Every instinct said wait a week, make it perfect. Instead I typed, “Rough draft. Please tell me where I'm going wrong,” and pressed send before my nerves could vote. My stomach fizzed for an hour. Ramesh, who edited the newsletter for years, phoned that evening. “The front page is good. Move the notices to the back. You do not need eight pages.” Two comments, and I had the shape of the whole thing. I wouldn't have found that alone in a month. Tomorrow I cut it to six. — Wasim

qa.q: What did the early feedback change about Wasim's plan?
qa.a: Ramesh's two comments, to move the notices to the back and cut the pages, gave Wasim the shape of the newsletter, so Wasim would cut it to six pages.

qa.a: Ramesh, who edited the newsletter for years, probably feels respected and pleased to be asked, and can give useful advice quickly.

grounding: A mature worker ships a good-enough draft, gets feedback and improves it rather than holding it for perfection.
